summary: @ornikar/eslint-config-react preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute hidden obfuscated payload
details: The package declares a `preinstall` hook (`node setup.mjs`) that, on `npm install`, downloads the Bun JavaScript runtime from a GitHub release URL, extracts it to a temporary directory, marks it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync` to run `math_init.js` — a 727KB heavily-obfuscated `@bun @bun-cjs` bundle shipped alongside the ESLint config. The bundle uses hex-mangled identifiers and a rotating string-array decoder (`WV8StW`) and is not referenced by the package's `main` (`index.js`), so it is only reachable through the preinstall-spawned Bun process. The manifest describes the package as an ESLint React config, and `main` is a plain FlatCompat ESLint export — nothing in the stated purpose requires an alternate JS runtime or an opaque 727KB payload at install time. Executing an obfuscated bundle under a non-Node runtime spawned from preinstall is arbitrary code execution on the installer's machine and also evades Node-based install-time scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
